title: Blockchain-based Privacy-Preserving Data Trading Using NFT and GANs
summary: Proposes a consortium-blockchain data marketplace in which datasets are registered as non-fungible tokens for ownership attribution and traded through a sealed-bid auction, with buyers receiving differentially private synthetic tables rather than the raw records. DP-CTGAN, the differentially private CTGAN variant, is the generative engine the framework runs: it is retrained on historical plus newly auctioned data at each settlement, its conditional probability sampling is what the design relies on to handle categorical imbalance, and it is evaluated on Adult, Census and Credit at a privacy budget chosen by sensitivity analysis.
affiliations: Guangzhou Vocational College of Science and Technology
evidence: the delivery and settlement step states the data exchange uses the DP-CTGAN model to retrain on both historical and newly acquired data; the framework section states it integrates differentially private generative models inspired by DPGAN and PATE-GAN and particularly DP-CTGAN, with categorical imbalance mitigated through conditional probability sampling; Figure 3 diagrams DP-CTGAN training and the evaluation uses Adult, Census and Credit. Note the model run is a third-party CTGAN derivative rather than CTGAN itself
needs: confirm the ruling for running a named third-party CTGAN derivative as the core engine: api_user or inherited

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Fraud Detection in Distributed Banking Networks
summary: Argues that federated GAN training across banks is unstable and that centralised fraud models breach data-sharing rules, and proposes keeping synthesis local while federating only the downstream classifier under differential privacy, with the privacy budget split between the two stages. CTGAN is the local synthesiser each client runs unmodified: it generates the balanced fraud records the classifier trains on, its variational Gaussian mixture transformer and conditional vector are carried into the framework's notation, and one half of the split privacy budget is spent on it, so the reported detection performance rests on what it produces.
evidence: the abstract states the framework integrates conditional tabular generative adversarial networks with differentially private federated learning and maintains local CTGAN synthesis while federating only the downstream classifier; the nomenclature defines the split privacy budgets as one for CTGAN and one for FedAvg and lists variational Gaussian mixture and TVAE; the related-work gap analysis contrasts the design with DP-CTGAN and PATE-GAN, and the contributions claim a novel combination of local CTGAN synthesis with federated learning

title: AI Surrogate Model for Distributed Computing Workloads
summary: Collects more than two million user-analysis job records over 150 days from the workload manager of a large physics computing grid and asks whether a generative model can stand in for that trace, so that data placement and payload allocation policies can be trained without the real submission records. Four tabular generators are trained and compared on per-feature distributions, pairwise feature correlations and distance to the closest record; TVAE, released alongside CTGAN, is one of them, and the paper reports it and CTABGAN+ missing the multi-peaked workload distribution that the diffusion and oversampling baselines track.
evidence: the abstract states that four generative models for tabular data, TVAE, CTABGAN+, SMOTE and TabDDPM, were applied to the collected job records; section IV.A describes TVAE as using a variational autoencoder as the backbone for learning and synthesising mixed-type tabular data; Figure 4 and Table I report TVAE failing to model the multi-peaked workload feature and give its Wasserstein distance, Jensen-Shannon divergence, correlation difference and distance-to-closest-record scores

title: Generating Realistic and Structured IoT Network Traffic Data with AMC-GAN
summary: Observes that IoT flow attributes such as protocol, port, connection state and payload length carry the semantics distinguishing benign from malicious traffic, and that a discriminator judging samples globally lets the generator produce locally inconsistent rows, then proposes AMC-GAN, which quantile-transforms numeric features and groups features by correlation so those relationships are enforced during training. AMC-GAN is built on CTGAN: the paper describes it as the first CTGAN-based generative framework for IoT network traffic, keeps CTGAN's generator and discriminator pair and its conditional vector mechanism for encoded categorical attributes, and measures the result against a CTGAN baseline.
evidence: the contributions state that to the best of the authors' knowledge AMC-GAN is the first CTGAN-based generative framework for IoT network traffic; section on the architecture states AMC-GAN builds on the CTGAN architecture by employing a generator and discriminator pair; the feature-processing section incorporates categorical features through CTGAN's conditional vector mechanism; the results report lower synthetic distinguishability under a C2ST classifier than a CTGAN baseline

title: A Dual Imbalanced Classification Framework With Feature Transfer Guided by Memory Compensation Strategy
summary: Targets imbalanced classification where the classes overlap rather than merely differ in size, arguing that generators and classifiers which lean on distribution information alone cannot separate samples in the overlapping region, and proposes transferring discriminative features under a memory compensation strategy that retains information about earlier samples. CTGAN is one of the data-level methods the framework is compared against across three classifiers, credited for introducing a conditional generator to capture the distribution of discrete columns that traditional GANs handle poorly.
